name: Elon Musk
current_role: CEO of Tesla and of SpaceX (which absorbed xAI in February 2026 and went public in June 2026)
summary: Elon Musk co-founded X.com in 1999, which merged with Confinity to form PayPal; he was replaced as CEO in 2000 but was its largest shareholder when eBay bought it. He founded SpaceX in 2002, became Tesla's chairman in 2004 and CEO in 2008, bought Twitter in 2022 (renamed X), and merged his AI company xAI into SpaceX in 2026 ahead of a record IPO. He spent at least $250 million backing Trump in 2024, led DOGE in 2025, then feuded publicly with Trump before returning to fund Republicans in the 2026 midterms.

connections.name: Peter Thiel
connections.description: After Musk's X.com merged with Thiel's Confinity in 2000, the board replaced Musk as CEO with Thiel in late 2000 while Musk was away on his honeymoon. Fortune later reported Musk had made up with the "mutineers."

connections.name: Peter Thiel
connections.description: Thiel's Founders Fund invested $20 million in SpaceX in 2008, its first institutional backer, a stake that paid off in SpaceX's June 2026 IPO; Thiel had declined to invest in Tesla. Founders Fund also backed the Boring Company and Neuralink.

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: Musk spent at least $250 million backing Trump in 2024, mainly through America PAC (other counts run higher), then led DOGE in 2025. Axios reported in July 2026 that he planned heavy spending for Republicans in the midterms.

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: In June 2025, after Musk left DOGE, a public feud over Trump's tax-and-spending bill led Trump to threaten Musk's government contracts and Musk to claim Trump would have lost without him. Musk later returned to funding Republicans.

sources.title: How Trump and Musk went from bromance to bitter dispute — Axios

connections.name: Larry Ellison
connections.description: Ellison calls Musk a "very close" friend. He held about $1 billion of Tesla stock, sat on Tesla's board from December 2018 to 2022 under the company's SEC settlement, and committed $1 billion to Musk's 2022 Twitter takeover.

connections.name: Marco Rubio
connections.description: Worked in parallel on dismantling USAID in early 2025: Musk's DOGE drove the cuts while Rubio, as acting administrator, canceled most of its contracts. The AP reported contradictory orders fueled talk of a power struggle, which both men denied.

connections.name: Reid Hoffman
connections.description: In 2024 Musk publicly accused Hoffman of being close to Jeffrey Epstein; Hoffman called it "a conviction with no evidence" and said he needed added security. Later-released documents showed Hoffman had an established relationship with Epstein, which he says he regrets; he denies being an Epstein client.

connections.name: Marc Andreessen
connections.description: In April 2022 Andreessen messaged Musk on Signal offering to co-invest in the Twitter buyout, and Andreessen Horowitz committed about $400 million; after the 2024 election Andreessen helped recruit staff for Musk's DOGE, which he called unpaid volunteer work. Andreessen's firm has also invested in xAI and SpaceX.

connections.name: Sam Altman
connections.description: After leaving OpenAI, Musk launched the rival xAI and in 2024 sued Altman and OpenAI over its shift to a for-profit model, seeking up to $134 billion; on May 18, 2026 a jury found the claims time-barred. Musk said he would appeal.

connections.description: Vance and Musk had a good relationship and spoke regularly even before Vance became Trump's running mate. During the June 2025 Trump–Musk feud Vance called Musk's attacks a "huge mistake" but hoped he would return to the fold, and with Susie Wiles he helped broker a thaw.
